source: ARCHITECTURE.md §4 'Type relation matrix' (identical to the data insert in now-db migration 0001), plus the `unknown` row added by F49 (PROGRESS.md) -- not in migration 0001's baseline insert, back-filled into every city by seed_city()'s ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING instead of a schema migration, since it is data, not DDL. `competes_with` added by now-db migration 0008 (Edition 2, 2026-09-24) -- see that migration's docstring for why the LIVE eat/drink rows needed an explicit data step rather than relying on this seed file's own ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING back-fill.
target: engine.type_relations in EVERY city database (per-site copy = per-site overridable in place; no deploy).
seed_policy: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (type) DO NOTHING — the seed never overwrites a row, so a site's edits are never clobbered. Changing a default here only affects rows that do not exist yet; to change an existing site, UPDATE its row directly. Every L1 `type` term in the platform vocabulary gets a row; a type with no entry below gets `unknown_type_default` (the strictest policy).
invariant: Exclusion is a property of `type`, never of partnership tier. Free, listed and paid partners get identical treatment (§4, §8.A, §11) — only link rendering differs.
venue_symmetry_rule: The six VENUE types (stay, eat, drink, wellness, shop, do) are mutually complementary -- if A may be suggested on a B page, B may be suggested on an A page. Row 1's job is literally 'a different type' (ARCHITECTURE.md §8), so an asymmetry here is an oversight, not curation. Hansel, 2026-09-11, after seeing it live: 'when a restaurant page is open, never suggest another restaurant. always hotel or other thing.' The original matrix had `stay` listing `eat` but `eat` NOT listing `stay`, so hotel pages showed restaurants while restaurant pages could never show hotels -- `complements` is a strict whitelist (`type = ANY(complements)` in row1_complementary.py), so the omission was a hard structural exclusion, not a ranking preference. `event` and `editorial` are deliberately NOT part of this closure: they are cross-cutting rather than venue competitors, and both carry `exclude_same: false`.
competes_with_rule: 2026-09-24 (docs/EDITION-2-PLAN.md §1), the owner drew the venue-symmetry rule above narrower than the data expressed it: 'never restaurant, cafe or F&B' means `eat` and `drink` are ONE competitive class, not two complementary ones -- a bar must not be suggested on a restaurant story and vice versa, even though they are different L1 types. `exclude_same` cannot express this (it only ever adds a type's OWN name to its excluded set); `competes_with` is the second, narrower axis: a per-row list of OTHER L1 types this type must never co-recommend, unioned into the excluded set unconditionally by `now_filters.type_relations.excluded_types_for` (see that function). Adding `eat`/`drink` here also required REMOVING each from the other's `complements` below -- the pairing the 2026-09-11 venue-symmetry fix had added is exactly the one pairing this narrower rule takes back out; every other complements pairing that fix added is untouched.
rail_priority_rule: 2026-09-24, second pass. `complements` gained a SECOND reader: `apps/web/src/lib/recommendSql.ts#complementSectionsFor` walks it in array order and takes the first-occurring SECTION per type (`lib/payload.ts#TYPE_TO_SECTION` -- eat/drink -> dining, do/shop -> things-to-do, stay -> stay, wellness -> wellness, event -> events) as its 'plan around it' rail display priority, capped at 3 rails. Same membership as before this pass (now-db migration 0010); only array POSITION changed, for exactly the 5 venue types below. Reasoning per type is in that migration's own docstring -- in short: stay -> dining, things-to-do, wellness (the coordinator's own example: 'Hotel: eat & drink, things to do, unwind'); eat -> stay, things-to-do, events ('Restaurant: stay, things to do, what's on' -- wellness drops out of the top 3); drink -> stay, things-to-do, wellness; wellness -> dining, stay, things-to-do; shop -> dining, stay, things-to-do.
